source_snapshot.procedure: Run `openbmctool.py ... ldap privilege-mapper delete --groupName=<groupName>` after generic prechecks/log clearing.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL preserves the named delete action but uses credential-bearing connection syntax, assumes DN/CN interchangeability, treats HTTP status as deletion proof and omits unique mapping resolution, affected role/user/session impact, unrelated-map preservation and recovery.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION with CRITICAL risk correctly requires exact mapping/group identity, complete inventory, pinned method, one approved delete, affected/control/local authorization tests, independent recovery and an optional separately approved restore.

old_problem: A group name alone may be ambiguous across realm/case/DN/nesting or may match the only administrative mapping. Command success does not prove that exactly one mapper entry disappeared, that the directory group stayed intact, that cached/active sessions follow policy, that affected users lost only intended rights, or that unrelated and local recovery access remained. These missing runtime bindings previously kept the review pending.
disposition_reason: The source-named tool documents a discrete privilege-mapper delete command, so the Review layer can define a safe parameterized one-relation deletion without guessing the group. Bind a canonical unique mapping and session policy, preserve a full inventory, delete once after approval, prove exact persisted and effective authorization impact, preserve the directory object and unrelated mappings, and restore only under separate approval. Project identities and policy values are readiness inputs, not unresolved engineering logic.
decision_basis: XLSX row 931, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, adjacent Add/List-Mapping rows and preserved V3.1 record were directly reviewed; row 932 and its manifest identity were independently verified.

Pinned openbmctool documentation defines separate privilege-mapper create, delete and list actions. The source delete therefore targets the BMC mapping relation, not the LDAP directory group and not every mapping for a user.

OpenBMC user-management architecture separates LDAP group membership, BMC privilege roles and interface/channel authorization. Persisted absence and real authorization/session effects require independent evidence.
ED-03/ED-13 and ED-33 through ED-38 support a parameterized BMC command contract while preserving exact source action, explicit approval, recovery and engineer-owned execution verdict.

test_case.test_name: Delete exactly one canonical LDAP privilege mapping and verify bounded authorization impact
test_case.purpose: Verify that a pinned openbmctool removes exactly one approved canonical LDAP-group-to-BMC-role mapping, that affected users lose the intended new-session authorization according to Project policy, that unrelated groups/mappings and the directory group itself remain unchanged, that active sessions follow the pre-approved rule, and that local/console recovery and exact optional restoration remain available.
required_package: Target BMC/firmware identity, supported role schema and pinned reviewed openbmctool/openbmc-tools commit
Canonical group DN/CN, realm, case and nesting semantics plus a unique mapping identity/role and proof that exactly one entry matches
Complete redacted mapping inventory correlated with directory membership, affected/control/local accounts, roles and named active sessions
Project authorization matrix for affected new login, unrelated/control user and local administrator, plus explicit retain/revoke expectation for existing sessions
Proof the target is not the only administrative/recovery path, protected credentials and independently tested local-admin/console recovery
Mapping backup, one-delete approval, directory-group non-deletion guard and separately approved exact recreate/restore plan
test_case.test_command: CRITICAL AUTHORIZATION REMOVAL; DO NOT EXECUTE WITHOUT POINT-OF-ACTION APPROVAL. Preserve security logs, pin/review openbmctool and capture the complete redacted mapping/account/membership/session baseline. Resolve the literal `groupName` to one canonical group and exactly one BMC mapping; stop on zero/multiple matches or if it is the sole admin/recovery relation. Bind expected affected/control/local new-login permissions and active-session behavior. After approval, run exactly one protected `ldap privilege-mapper delete --groupName=<canonical approved value>`. Capture redacted response/audit and list/read back the full inventory to prove only the target relation is absent. Confirm the LDAP directory group and membership are unchanged. From independent sessions, verify affected-user access reduction/denial, unrelated/control continuity, local-admin recovery and the approved existing-session behavior. Recreate the mapping only under separate approval using its exact saved group/role. Never bulk-delete, change directory membership, clear logs or retry automatically.
test_case.expected_result: Exactly the approved group-to-role relation is absent from persistent BMC mappings and every unrelated mapping is byte/field equivalent to baseline; the LDAP directory group and membership remain unchanged. Affected new authentication loses precisely the deleted mapping's authorization, unrelated/control users retain expected access, local administration remains available and named existing sessions follow the approved policy. The final state is either the approved deletion state or an exactly restored mapping with independent readback and audit evidence.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires unique canonical target proof, approval, one delete, audit plus full before/after inventory showing only one relation changed, directory non-deletion, affected/control/local effective-authorization results, approved session behavior and final-state/optional-restore proof. Tool output or HTTP status alone cannot pass. Wrong/ambiguous mapping, unrelated change, directory-group or membership change, unexpected privilege/session behavior, local-access loss, secret exposure, restore failure or residual mismatch is FAIL and stops. Missing identity, policy, recovery, tool or approval is NOT READY rather than Engineering Decision Pending.
safety_gate: Require exact canonical group and a unique BMC mapping match; never delete using an ambiguous short name or wildcard.
Do not delete the only administrative/recovery mapping, the LDAP directory group, directory membership, multiple mappings or unrelated sessions.
Prove local-admin and independent console recovery first and preserve complete redacted inventory and security logs.
Protect BMC/test credentials from URLs, history, process listings, logs, screenshots and records; use dedicated affected/control test identities where possible.
Run one delete only. Stop on timeout, access loss, unexpected session/role or inventory change; do not retry or bulk-recreate.
expected_evidence: Approval, target/firmware, pinned tool commit/hash, canonical group/mapping/role and unique-match proof
Complete redacted mapping, directory membership, affected/control/local account and named-session baseline plus independent recovery proof
One protected delete response/audit and full post-delete inventory proving only the target relation changed
Directory group/membership unchanged, affected-user access reduction, unrelated/control continuity, local-admin continuity and approved active-session behavior
Approved final deletion state or separately approved exact mapping recreation/readback, preserved logs/secrets and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: If the wrong or multiple mappings are affected, access/session behavior is unexpected or local recovery degrades, stop without another delete. Use independent local-admin/console access to recreate only the verified saved group-to-role relation under separate approval, reconcile the entire inventory, close/revoke test sessions according to policy, preserve audit evidence and rotate exposed credentials. Do not alter the directory group or bulk-recreate mappings.

source_conflict.reason: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require deleting a named privilege mapping. Exact group resolution, role effect and session policy are parameterized execution inputs, not competing source purposes.

blocked.reason: The one-relation delete, evidence, impact verification and recovery contract are defined. Target mapping identities and policy values can be bound safely before execution.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: Target schema/tool commit; canonical unique group/mapping; affected/control/local authorization and active-session matrix; complete baseline; recovery path; one-delete and optional restore approvals.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; CRITICAL AUTHORIZATION REMOVAL; POINT-OF-ACTION APPROVAL REQUIRED; NO MAPPING OR DIRECTORY STATE CHANGED
